metaTitle: Student Accommodation in Murcia: Erasmus Housing Guide
metaDescription: Erasmus in Murcia or Cartagena? Where to live near UMU, UCAM and UPCT, what to check in the contract, how to avoid scams and book a room.
h1: Student Accommodation in Murcia: The Erasmus and International Student Housing Guide
intro: Finding a room in Murcia as an Erasmus or international student is very doable, but it goes better if you know the city before you land. This guide covers where to live near UMU, UCAM and UPCT, which type of accommodation suits you, what to check before you sign and how to spot a rental scam. It comes from InterRoom Murcia, an agency that rents rooms to students in Murcia and Cartagena every year. If you want a person to help you, message us on WhatsApp at +34 614 33 19 65.

sections.h2: Why Murcia works well for Erasmus students
sections.content:
Murcia is a mid-sized city with a flat centre, a lot of sun and a student life that revolves around its universities. You can get around by bike, tram or on foot, and nothing in the city is far away. That makes arriving without a car much easier than in a big capital.

There are three universities in the area. The Universidad de Murcia (UMU) has its main campus in Espinardo and faculties in the centre. UCAM is the private Catholic university on the Guadalupe side. The UPCT, the technical university, sits in the old town of Cartagena, about 50 km away on the coast.

All three have an international office that handles Erasmus and exchange students, and all three can point you to housing help. The practical part is deciding where to live before you commit to a rent.
sections.highlight: Pick your area by campus first. Your daily commute matters more than the neighbourhood's looks.

sections.h2: When to start looking for a room
sections.content:
For an autumn start, begin looking two to three months ahead and decide on a plan B for your first nights. For a spring semester, start around the end of the previous autumn term. Good rooms near campus go first.

You do not need to sign a long contract blind. Many students book a hostel or short stay for the first days, then visit rooms in person. UPCT's international office suggests this for Cartagena and has an agreement with a local hostel for newcomers. UMU's housing service, VIMUR, also handles stays of under three months.

If you cannot travel to view rooms, ask for a live video call of the actual room, not just photos. Message InterRoom Murcia on WhatsApp (https://wa.me/34614331965) and we will tell you what is available for your dates.

sections.h2: Where to live: UMU, UCAM and UPCT areas
sections.content:
UMU (Espinardo and La Merced): the Espinardo campus is served by Murcia's tram line 1, so living in or near Espinardo puts you close to classes. Living in the centre, around La Merced, is more lively and has more bars and shops. In return you will rely on the tram or bus for the campus run, so check the route and the timetable before you choose.

UCAM (Guadalupe and La Ñora): these two areas are the closest to the UCAM campus, and some students can walk. They are quieter and less central. UCAM's own accommodation guide describes the centre as more convenient for leisure but with a longer journey to campus.

UPCT (Cartagena centre): the university is in the old town, so a room in the casco antiguo means walking to class. It is compact, near the port and the Roman sites.
sections.highlight: A cheap room far from your campus costs you time and transport money every day.

sections.h2: Shared flat, room or residence: which is right for you
sections.content:
Shared flat or room: the most common choice for exchange students. You rent a bedroom and share kitchen and bathroom with other students. It is usually the cheaper route and you meet people quickly. The downside is that bills, house rules and flatmates vary a lot, so ask what is included before you pay.

Residence: you get a furnished room, often with services and a simpler booking process. It costs clearly more than a room in a flat and can be less flexible, but it is easy if you want everything in one place. UMU lists private residences and a Colegio Mayor, and UPCT points to a residence run through a partner operator.

UMU's official housing page also lists VIMUR, HousingAnywhere, Erasmusu and MiCampus. Look in our InterRoom Murcia catalogue, filterable by university and area, for rooms near your campus.
sections.highlight: Rooms in shared flats suit most Erasmus students, and residences suit those who want a simple, all-in arrangement.

sections.h2: Contract, deposit and budget: what to check
sections.content:
Spanish rental law sets the deposit (fianza). Under the Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos, a housing lease requires a cash deposit of one month's rent. Any extra guarantee the landlord asks for is limited by law, so a request for several months up front is a reason to ask questions.

Before you sign, read the contract for the start and end dates, the exact rent, which bills are included, and how the deposit is returned. Get a signed copy and a receipt for every payment.

Budget: monthly rent is only part of it. Add electricity, water, internet and your own food and transport. Rents change every year and vary by area, so ask for the full monthly cost in writing. We give you the total figure for each room at InterRoom Murcia.
sections.highlight: By law, the deposit for a housing lease is one month's rent. Ask for a receipt.

sections.h2: How to avoid rental scams when you search from abroad
sections.content:
Foreign students are a favourite target, because they often pay before seeing the room. INCIBE, Spain's cybersecurity institute, lists the classic warning signs: a price far below the market, photos copied from other websites, and a landlord who is abroad and cannot show the property.

Other red flags: pressure to pay quickly, requests to pay through anonymous money transfer services, and a company email address from a free provider. Never send money for a place you have not seen, or at least verified on a live video call with someone who can prove they are the landlord or agent.

Search the address and the owner's name, and check the photos match the street. If anything feels off, stop. If you want a second opinion on an offer, send it to us on WhatsApp at +34 614 33 19 65 and we will tell you what we think.
sections.highlight: A price that looks too good, a landlord who is always abroad and a demand for fast payment are the three classic warning signs.

faq.question: Where do Erasmus students usually live in Murcia?
faq.answer: Most rent a room in a shared flat with other students. Many choose the Espinardo area for UMU, Guadalupe or La Ñora for UCAM, and the old town for UPCT in Cartagena. InterRoom Murcia can show you rooms for each campus.

faq.question: Can I find accommodation before I arrive in Murcia?
faq.answer: Yes, but be careful. UMU's VIMUR service and UCAM's accommodation database can help, and agencies like InterRoom Murcia can arrange viewings by video call. Avoid paying for a room you have not seen or checked.

faq.question: How much is the deposit for a room in Spain?
faq.answer: For a housing lease, Spanish law (LAU, article 36) sets the deposit at one month's rent. Ask for it in writing and for a receipt, and check how it is returned when you leave.

faq.question: Is it better to live in a residence or a shared flat?
faq.answer: A shared flat is usually cheaper and more flexible, while a residence is simpler and all-in. Think about your budget, the length of your stay and how much privacy you want.

faq.question: Can I get to the UCAM or UMU campus from the centre of Murcia?
faq.answer: Yes. Murcia has a tram line that serves the area around the Espinardo campus and a branch towards UCAM, and there are buses too. Check the timetable and the fares on the tram operator's website before choosing a room.
